title: Idempotence of the 0–1 indicator function
statement: Let $B$ be a set of $n$-bit Boolean inputs, and let $\mathbf{1}_B \colon (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}) \to \bbr$ be its indicator function, taking the value $1$ at points of $B$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then for every $n$-bit Boolean input $y$, \[ \bigl(\mathbf{1}_B(y)\bigr)^2 = \mathbf{1}_B(y). \]
hypotheses_covered: B is a set of n-bit Boolean inputs
y is an n-bit Boolean input
the indicator uses the constant value 1 on B and 0 off B
replaced:
For any set $B \subseteq \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$ and $y : \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$, the
indicator function satisfies $(\mathbf{1}_B(y))^2 = \mathbf{1}_B(y)$.
